submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 with iterative topological clustering and learned calibration at 35 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 94.028% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents a significant performance advantage over Algorithm-L3 (85.4% at 35 GeV) and Algorithm-L2 (74.4% at 35 GeV). Extensive threshold scans were performed for all three algorithms across the allowed 20-60 GeV range, confirming that 35 GeV is the optimal operating point for Algorithm-L1. All candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget, making Algorithm-L1 deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware. The superior performance of Algorithm-L1 is consistent with the 2025 simulation summary and makes it the clear choice for maximizing signal efficiency while respecting all constraints.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV achieves 94.028% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, which is the highest among all tested configurations across all three candidate algorithms and threshold values.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates listed: Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: All three candidate algorithms, including Algorithm-L1, fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs) as documented in the candidate specifications.
The recommended threshold of 35 GeV falls within the allowed range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Operate at the allocated trigger rate of 8 kHz
requirements.evidence: All simulations were performed at the allocated 8 kHz rate as specified in the rate allocation document. The efficiency results are reported at this rate.
